guideTitle: Best Dehumidifiers for 1,500 Sq Ft Spaces (2026)
metaDescription: Six compressor dehumidifiers sized for 1,500 square feet compared on pint rating, drain options, noise and Energy Star status for basements and open floors.
expertTake: The Midea Cube 20 pint is the pick for a 1,500 square foot basement because it states a sensible rating and carries Energy Star certification. The Trazico 21 pint is the value pick with a hose and three modes. Buyers with a very wet space should step up a size instead of trusting a 1,500 square foot label.
introParagraphs: At 1,500 square feet you are in the sweet spot for household compressor dehumidifiers. The machines in this class are compact, portable and rated for a whole basement or a large open floor, and they are the most heavily marketed size on the shelf.

That popularity also invites inflated numbers. Two machines with the same coverage label can differ by a third in water removal, and some quote ratings on a scale that no longer matches the current test. The goal here is to separate the realistic machines from the optimistic ones.

products.name: Midea Cube 20 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier, 1,500 sq ft
products.description:
Midea's Cube is a compact, boxy compressor machine designed to stand on a floor and stay out of the way. Its 20 pint rating on the current scale lines up with a 1,500 square foot space of moderate dampness, which is the standard sizing table behind most household units. A modest rating that matches the room is better than a big number that does not.

Energy Star certification means more water removed per kilowatt hour than a standard unit, and over a humid summer the saving is real. The listing says the tank is up to three times larger than the previous design, which cuts emptying trips, and a drain hose option removes them entirely. Against the Trazico at 21 pints, the Midea is rated one pint lower but carries the efficiency label and a better-known service network.

Keep the filter clean, vacuum the coil yearly and leave a hand's width of clearance. Compressors in this class often run 5 to 10 years when treated well. It is the straightforward pick for a basement with moderate moisture. Set the humidistat to 45 percent for the first week, check the result with a separate meter, and then nudge it by a few points. Placing the unit in the middle of the space rather than in a corner lets the intake draw from more of the room, which usually shortens the time to reach the target.
products.bestFor: A moderately damp 1,500 square foot basement that needs efficient, steady running.
pros: Rated 20 pints on the current scale
cons: One pint below the 21 pint rivals

products.name: Trazico 21 Pint Dehumidifier with Drain Hose, 1,500 sq ft
products.description:
Trazico is a no-frills compressor unit with a 21 pint rating, a drain hose and three targeted modes. The modes let you hold a humidity target, run flat out or dry laundry, which covers the usual household uses. A continuous drain keeps a wet basement from filling the bucket every day.

Its rating is one pint above the Midea, but it lacks the Energy Star label, so it costs a little more to run per pint. Against the Dravonic units, the Trazico is plainer and has less published detail on defrost and noise. The tradeoff is simplicity: fewer features to fail and a lower purchase tier.

Over the long run the filter and the drain hose are the usual wear points. Replace a hose that has gone stiff, and rinse the tank when you use it. It is the value choice for someone who wants a plain, capable machine.
products.bestFor: A basement or open floor where a simple machine with a hose is enough.
pros: 21 pint rating at a restrained tier
Simple controls with little to fail
cons: Noise claim is a marketing term

products.name: Dravonic 21 Pint Compressor Dehumidifier with Auto Defrost
products.description:
Dravonic puts the word compressor in the headline and then backs it with auto defrost, which is the feature a cool basement actually needs. At temperatures near 60 degrees a coil frosts and the unit stops removing water, so a defrost cycle keeps the machine working in the conditions where basements live. A 40 dB listing figure is also low for this class.

The 0.4 gallon tank is small, which means you will want the hose in a damp room, since the tank would fill in hours. Against the Trazico, the Dravonic adds the defrost and the noise figure but has the same 21 pint rating. The smart humidity control holds a target you set across its three modes.

Clean the filter monthly and wipe the humidity sensor. Keep the hose slope clear so water does not pool at a low point. It is the better choice for a cool, unheated basement. When you set it up, run the hose in a continuous downhill line to the drain and tape it down so it cannot sag into a trap. If the basement has a sump pit nearby, the hose can often discharge there, which removes the need for any pump at all.
products.bestFor: A cool, unheated basement where defrost matters.
pros: Smart humidity control with three modes
cons: Hose is nearly mandatory in a damp room

products.name: PLUSCENT 21 Pint Dehumidifier with Laundry Acceleration
products.description:
PLUSCENT builds its identity around a laundry acceleration mode that runs the fan and compressor harder to dry clothes on a rack. A dehumidifier can dry a load of laundry faster than a closed room, and a dedicated mode makes it a one-button job. If the machine will live in a laundry area or a basement with a drying line, that feature is practical.

It shares the 21 pint rating with the Trazico and Dravonic, so the difference is feature mix. Dual drainage and an auto shutoff give it the safety of the group. Compared with the Midea, it lacks the Energy Star mark but adds the laundry mode.

Rinse the tank, clean the filter and keep clothes a couple of feet from the intake. It suits a household that uses the machine for both room drying and clothes.
products.bestFor: A laundry room or basement where clothes dry on a rack.
cons: Feature set overlaps with cheaper units

products.name: HXCOCKCROW 34 Pint Dehumidifier with Drain Hose
products.description:
HXCOCKCROW lists 34 pints a day for the same 1,500 square foot label, which looks like a big step above the 21 pint machines. The likely explanation is the test scale: older and looser conditions give higher pint numbers for the same hardware. A 34 pint claim and a 21 pint claim can describe machines of similar real output.

The unit includes a drain hose and a child safety lock, which is useful in a household where a basement machine sits within reach. Against the Midea, the HXCOCKCROW has the bigger label and fewer certifications to back it. Treat the number as a ceiling rather than a promise.

Rinse the filter, keep the hose clear and check the lock before leaving it with children. It works when you want the larger rated number and a hose, as long as you accept the uncertainty behind it.
products.bestFor: A household with children where a lockable panel matters.
pros: Highest listed pint rating of the group
cons: Rating likely uses a looser test scale

products.name: 30 Pint Compact Smart Dehumidifier with App and 24H Timer
products.description:
This model's headline is size: the listing describes a very compact body for a 30 pint rating. A smaller case is easier to tuck into a closet or utility corner and easier to carry upstairs. App control and a 24 hour timer let you schedule it for cheap electricity hours or while you are away.

The 1.6 liter tank is small, roughly 0.4 gallons, so the drain hose is the real drainage plan. Against the HXCOCKCROW at 34 pints, it is slightly lower on paper and more convenient to schedule. Like the other high-number listings, the 30 pint figure is probably on a generous test scale.

Expect to rinse the filter monthly and confirm the on-unit humidistat works without the app. Smart features can lapse with cloud changes. Scheduling in a small body is the reason to buy it.
products.bestFor: A small utility area where scheduling and a compact body matter.
cons: Small 1.6 L tank needs the hose
30 pint rating is probably a generous scale

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 1,500 square foot moderately damp space matches the 20 to 22 pint class on the current US test at 65 degrees and 60 percent humidity. The Midea at 20 pints and the Trazico at 21 pints both fit that range. A 34 pint label like the HXCOCKCROW's probably uses a looser scale, so do not read it as a bigger machine.

A basement near 60 degrees ices a coil quickly, and the machine then idles. The Dravonic lists auto defrost, which keeps it working in that range. A unit without defrost will cycle and lose output in an unheated space.

A 0.4 gallon tank on the Dravonic or a 1.6 liter tank on the compact smart unit fills in hours in a damp basement. A drain hose turns the machine into a set-and-forget appliance. Plan the hose route before you plan the purchase.

A unit that runs eight hours a day for months multiplies any efficiency gap. The Midea's Energy Star certification means more water removed per kilowatt hour. Efficiency is measured in liters per kilowatt hour, with about 1.6 or better as a good target.

A compressor and fan make steady sound, and 40 dB on the Dravonic is a low listed figure for the class. If the unit sits near a bedroom or workshop, noise matters more than coverage. Place it with clearance so airflow stays quiet.
A laundry mode on the PLUSCENT or app scheduling on the compact smart unit add convenience. They do not change water removal. Choose them only if you will actually use them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating realism
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pint ratings against the 20 to 22 pint class that fits 1,500 square feet on the current scale. The Midea at 20 and the Trazico at 21 sat in that range. The 30 and 34 pint listings were treated as claims on a looser scale.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cool-room performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for defrost features and operating range from the spec sheet. The Dravonic's auto defrost earned credit. Units that did not mention defrost were assumed to need a warmer space.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked hose inclusion and tank size. The 0.4 gallon Dravonic tank and the 1.6 liter compact unit both rely on the hose. A machine with a hose and a larger tank scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency and noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted Energy Star status for the Midea and the 40 dB listing for the Dravonic. Owner feedback patterns on noise shaped the ranks. Efficiency matters most for a machine that runs all season.

howWeEvaluated.title: Feature value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed laundry modes, child locks and app scheduling against their cost. They help specific buyers but do not change core drying. Features were used as tie-breakers, not as the main criterion.

cards.label: Energy Star
cards.text: The Midea Cube is certified, so it removes more water per kilowatt hour. Over a long humid season the saving is real. It costs a little more to buy.

cards.label: Standard
cards.text: The Trazico, PLUSCENT and HXCOCKCROW carry no certification. They cost less up front and a bit more to run. They suit seasonal or occasional use.

howToChoose.note: Choose Energy Star if the unit runs more than a few hours a day; otherwise a standard unit is fine.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Auto defrost, a hose drain and a rating in the 20 to 22 pint class on the current scale. Size one step up if the floor is below grade.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Dravonic 21 Pint is the cool-basement choice, with defrost and a quiet listing. The Midea Cube 20 Pint is the efficient pick for a warmer, finished lower level.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The machine runs all season or sits in a cool space. The Midea Cube and the Dravonic repay the premium in efficiency and reliable defrost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need seasonal drying only. The Trazico does the job without extras.

maintenance.why: A dusty filter cuts coil airflow, and frost shows up first on cool days. Rinse and dry it fully.
Standing water grows slime and odor. A quick wipe prevents buildup.
A kinked or sagging hose pools water and trips the unit off. Replace stiff or cloudy hose.
Dust on the fins raises power draw and cuts output. Use a soft brush.
Built-in sensors drift about 5 percent. A standalone hygrometer on a shelf confirms the 40 to 50 percent target.

faq.q: What size dehumidifier fits 1,500 square feet?
faq.a: A 20 to 22 pint machine on the current scale fits a moderately damp space. A very wet space needs the next size up.

faq.q: Why do some 1,500 square foot units list 34 pints?
faq.a: Older or looser test conditions give higher pint numbers for similar hardware. Compare the stated test condition, not only the number.
In a damp basement, yes. Small tanks of 0.4 gallons or 1.6 liters can fill in hours.

faq.q: How long does a compressor dehumidifier last?
faq.a: Typically 5 to 10 years. Clean filters and coils extend it.
For a machine that runs most of the day for months, yes. The saving accumulates each season.
Between 40 and 50 percent. Readings over 60 percent invite mold, while under 30 percent the air feels dry.
